header.running_head: Occupation with the Ahadeeth of Rasulullaah ﷺ and Befitting Behaviour for those Occupied with this

blocks.text: Hadhrat Suhayb (RA)'s Reluctance to say, "Rasulullaah ﷺ said"

Hadhrat Sulaymaan bin Abu Abdullaah reports that he heard Hadhrat Suhayb (RA) say, "By Allaah! I shall never intentionally narrate Ahadeeth to you saying that it is what Rasulullaah ﷺ said. However, I shall gladly relate to you what I experienced in the expeditions I participated in with Rasulullaah ﷺ. Then again, I shall never say, 'Rasulullaah ﷺ said'." [^1]
Hadhrat Waathila bin Asqa (RA) Narrates only the Intended Meaning of the Ahadeeth

Hadhrat Makhool relates, "Abul Azhar and I once went to Hadhrat Waathila bin Asqa (RA) and said, 'O Abu Asqa! Narrate to us a Hadith that you heard from Rasulullaah ﷺ without any uncertain words, and without any additions or omissions.' Hadhrat Waathila (RA) asked, 'Has any of you recited any part of the Qur'aan last night?' 'Yes,' we replied, 'But since we are not Huffaadh, we tend to add a Waaw (و) or an Alif (ا).'
To this, Hadhrat Waathila (RA) remarked, 'And that is the Qur'aan which you have still not mastered when it has been in your midst for such a long time. When you feel that you are adding or omitting letters to it, what about the Ahadeeth that we had perhaps heard only once from Rasulullaah ﷺ? It is sufficient for you that we narrate only their intended meanings to you." [^2]
Hadhrat Umar (RA) Censures those Sahabah (RA) who Narrated Plenty of Ahadeeth

blocks.narrator: Hadhrat Ibraheem bin Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf
blocks.text: Hadhrat Ibraheem bin Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf relates, "By Allaah! Before he passed away, Hadhrat Umar (RA) sent messengers to various distant places to summon Sahabah (RA) such as Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Hudhaafa (RA), Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA), Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) and Hadhrat Uqba bin Aamir (RA). When they had gathered, he said to them, 'What Ahadeeth have you people spread to even the far distant lands?' 'Are you forbidding us from narrating them?' they asked. 'No,' Hadhrat Umar (RA) replied, 'I just want you to remain with me. By Allaah! I do not want you to part from me (here in Madinah) for as long as I live because we know best which of your narrations we shall accept and which ones we will not.' They therefore did not part from Hadhrat Umar (RA) until he passed away." [^3]

Hadhrat Ibraheem bin Abdur Rahmaan relates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) sent for Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA), Hadhrat Abu Mas'ood Ansaari and Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) and said to them, "What are the Ahadeeth that you are so frequently narrating to the people?" He then confined them to Madinah until he was martyred. [^4]
